quote: I received a form you sold out.
stewart_read: The intro reference to the form is garbled/unclear ('sold out' likely a mis-transcription of 'filled out') and gives minimal legitimacy grounding before pivoting straight to the pitch.
coaching_implication: Slow down the intro line so the form reference lands clearly — legitimacy anchors need to be crisp, not rushed.

quote: you guys tell me this. You tell me nothing out of pocket.
stewart_read: This is a cost/trust objection early in the call; rather than flipping it against the customer's actual bill pain, the rep gives a flat literal reassurance.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is stronger — the rep never captured a bill or interest reason to flip against, so there was no bill anchor available to invert with.
coaching_implication: Even without a captured bill, rep could reframe: 'the thing costing you is your current electric bill, not this evaluation' — but that requires having asked about the bill first.

quote: So the way the program works is you would switch over to solar energy
stewart_read: Rep starts explaining the mechanics of the solar savings program to answer the cost objection instead of redirecting to the specialist earlier.
alternative_hypothesis: Some explanation is arguably necessary to resolve the trust objection in the moment; full redirect may have been too abrupt this early.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch line ('that's exactly what our specialist explains in detail') sooner instead of walking through program mechanics himself.

quote: If you're available, I can have my specialist bring that evaluation over. It'll take, like, thirty to forty five minutes,
stewart_read: Rep books the appointment on program mechanics rather than the customer's specific situation — no bill, no interest reason, no personalized hook was ever captured to create curiosity around.
coaching_implication: Without any qualify data, the appointment has no personalized pull; closer walks in blind on this customer's motivation.

quote: Great. I'll we'll meet with you tomorrow at 12:30,
stewart_read: No 'is that fair?' handshake, no one-hour block statement, no driving/computer instruction — button-up is incomplete per verified events (2/4 parts only).
coaching_implication: Add the missing button-up elements: hour block, no-driving/computer instruction, and the verbal handshake to reduce no-show risk.

stewart_read: Rep pivots to scheduling before ever asking what interested the customer in solar or capturing any qualification info per verified events (interest question skipped).
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: given this is a recycled lead where 'we never got a chance to get that evaluation to you,' rep may be trying to fast-track re-engagement rather than re-run full verify.
coaching_implication: Even on a recycled lead recovery call, at minimum capture the bill and interest reason before booking so the closer isn't walking in blind.
